newsitem.title: USA: Wash.-Canada power line restart delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Wash.-Canada power line restart delayed again.

text.p: Restart of the double-circuit 500 kilovolt Raver-Schultz power line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to Canada, was delayed again until the end of this week, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday.
The delay was attributed to continued cold, icy conditions in northern Washington, where an ice storm Jan 17 initially knocked the parallel lines out of service.
"We hope to have one line re-energized by Friday and the second by Sunday," a BPA spokeswoman said.
The federal power marketing agency has had to restrict hydroelectric power generation at certain dams due to voltage support concerns related to the transmission line outage.
But recent warmer weather for most areas of the Pacific Northwest has reduced demand for BPA's power, allowing the agency to offer surplus power during peak demand hours.
